chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfah, from Jamil, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The slave does not inherit, and the divorced woman does not inherit."

The explanation (resolution) of this report is that the slave does not inherit as long as there is a free person present; but in the absence of a free person, he does inherit, according to what we have previously established.
ai.seo_question: Does a slave inherit from his master if there are free heirs present?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to clarify the hierarchy of inheritance between slaves and free persons, noting that the exclusion of the slave applies only when a free heir exists. The term 'taliq' refers to a woman whose divorce is pending or finalized but not yet fully consummated in terms of inheritance rights, illustrating the nuanced application of kinship ties in early Islamic jurisprudence. This principle underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextual interpretation (ta'wil) of apparent contradictions in hadith regarding social status and inheritance shares.
